docs.text: Below Cleveland, in a subterranean world many surface dwellers don’t know exists, miners extract a crucial winter mineral — salt. The Whiskey Island salt mine helps supply road salt across the Northeast and Great Lakes, where a colder, snowier-than-usual winter has driven demand.

#maddow #inners
Science break.
Go 1,800 feet below Lake Erie into a network of mining tunnels that spans nearly 3 miles away from the Cleveland shoreline. Cargill mines nearly 4 million tons of salt annually for use on winter roads.

The largest salt mine in the world is the Sifto salt mine in Goderich, Ontario. The mine is 1,800 feet below Lake Huron. It produces over seven million tons of rock salt each year. The rock salt is used primarily for road de-icing, manufacturing, and water softeners.
